llm.summary: The skill's purpose (code generation) is plausible, but there are inconsistencies between its documentation and the packaged files (missing templates, no install/CLI wiring, declared dependency not installed) that should be resolved before trusting it.

dimensions.detail: Name, description, SKILL.md and scripts/generator.py all describe a code-generator and included code shows templates and file-writing logic consistent with that purpose. However, SKILL.md references a templates directory (references/templates/) and a CLI command (neckr0ik-code-generator) that are not present in the package manifest. The claw.json declares a dependency on pyyaml but there is no install spec to satisfy dependencies — these mismatches reduce coherence.
dimensions.label: Purpose & Capability
dimensions.name: purpose_capability

dimensions.detail: SKILL.md directs users/agents to run a CLI command (neckr0ik-code-generator) and to use templates in references/templates/. The packaged files only include scripts/generator.py and no templates directory. Instructions also show generating from external OpenAPI URLs (which implies network fetches) but there is no explicit mention of how network access is performed or which code will fetch remote specs. Because instructions require files/paths that are not present, the runtime behavior is unclear.
dimensions.label: Instruction Scope
dimensions.name: instruction_scope

dimensions.detail: No install spec is provided (instruction-only), yet claw.json lists a dependency (pyyaml). Without an install step, dependencies won't be automatically installed and the CLI name shown in SKILL.md is not wired to the included script. That mismatch could lead to accidental execution of the script in ad-hoc ways, or missing runtime dependencies.
dimensions.label: Install Mechanism
dimensions.name: install_mechanism

dimensions.detail: The skill does not request any environment variables, credentials, or config paths. The generator code shown writes files under an output directory, which is expected for a scaffolding tool and proportional to its purpose.
dimensions.label: Credentials
dimensions.name: environment_proportionality

dimensions.detail: The skill does not request always:true and does not claim elevated platform privileges. It is user-invocable and model invocation is allowed (normal for skills). No evidence it modifies other skills or global agent settings.
dimensions.label: Persistence & Privilege
dimensions.name: persistence_privilege

llm.guidance:
This skill appears to be a legitimate code generator, but there are several red flags you should resolve before installing or running it:

- SKILL.md refers to a CLI named neckr0ik-code-generator and to a references/templates/ directory, but the package only includes scripts/generator.py and no templates. Ask the author (or require) the missing templates and a reproducible install step.
- claw.json declares pyyaml as a dependency but there is no install script. Confirm how dependencies will be installed, and prefer a declared, auditable install mechanism (pip/requirements, or a vetted package) over ad-hoc instructions.
- Review the full scripts/generator.py (complete file) and any template files before running. Look for any network calls, unexpected file reads (e.g., reading ~/.ssh or system files), or code that executes shell commands. If generator will fetch OpenAPI specs from URLs, decide whether that network activity is acceptable and validate fetched content before using it in production code.
- Because templates are missing, do not run the script until you obtain the templates and confirm what will be written to disk. Run the generator in an isolated environment (container or VM) the first time.

What would change this assessment: providing the missing references/templates/ files, an explicit, safe install spec (or packaged CLI), and the full generator.py source (so we can verify there are no unexpected network/exfiltration behaviors). If those are provided and look clean, the skill would be coherent and likely benign.
